title: Input and Pesticide Compliance: Verify Before Use

content.overview: A cultivation input should be checked for crop/site authorization, label directions, worker-protection requirements and jurisdiction-specific restrictions before use. The safest educational rule is verify first rather than compiling a universal list that can become outdated or wrong across jurisdictions.

vocabulary.definition: The crop, site, rate, method and other conditions authorized or directed by a product label.
Entry into a treated area after application, subject to applicable safety and regulatory restrictions.
Documentation of product, date, location, amount, operator and other required application information.

sections.title: Availability is not authorization
sections.body: A product sold online or in a garden store may not be approved for every crop, production system or jurisdiction. Verify the actual label and current agency guidance.

sections.title: Worker rules are part of product use
sections.body: PPE, notification, reentry and decontamination requirements can affect how and when work occurs around an application.

sections.title: Keep evidence of the decision
sections.body: Application and label records support traceability, worker communication and later review. Recordkeeping also helps prevent repeated mistakes when rules or products change.

workedExamples: Before using a pest-control product recommended in a forum, check the current label and applicable agricultural/cannabis rules for the specific crop and site.
If a label changes between seasons, retain the version associated with each historical application record.
commonMistakes: Assuming natural or organic means unrestricted.
Using a product on a crop not listed or otherwise allowed by the applicable rules.
content.practicalApplication: Create a pre-use checklist covering product identity, label version, crop/site, intended use, PPE, reentry, worker communication, disposal and required records. Stop if authorization is unclear.
content.summary: Responsible input use is verification-driven. Product label, worker protection, jurisdiction and documentation all have to agree before application.
